findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - concurrent Forge runs hit a secondary limit while merge reads a pull request.
The new matcher requires `exceeded` after `rate limit` unless the status is 429. New evidence relative to the ruling is that GitHub also returns [HTTP 403 with “You have exceeded a secondary rate limit”](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4443). For `gh pr view`, the error is returned without a successful result on stdout, so neither alternative matches. The failure reaches `src/forge/merge.py:66`, and merge refuses instead of waiting. The previous matcher recognized `secondary rate limit`; the revised test at `tests/test_github_rate_limits_wait_for_reset.py:23` uses HTTP 429, which masks this regression.
findings.title: Functional: HTTP 403 secondary rate limits stop Forge commands
